title: Hybrid network consolidation
brief: Eighty VPCs, two data centers, overlapping acquired CIDRs, private DNS, and regulated inspection require a scalable connectivity plan.
must_address: Direct Connect plus diverse VPN recovery
trap: Full-mesh peering is non-transitive and operationally quadratic.

title: Cross-account security
brief: Workforce federation, vendor access, centralized detection, and independent log custody are required across business units.
must_address: IAM Identity Center and temporary roles
trap: SCPs bound permissions but do not grant them.

title: Tiered recovery
brief: Transaction intake requires 15-minute RPO and 1-hour RTO; analytics can tolerate 24 hours.
trap: Backup success is not restore evidence.

title: Organization design
brief: Autonomous product teams need guardrails, shared networking, central audit, and isolated production blast radius.
trap: One account with tags does not provide strong isolation.

title: Cost attribution
brief: Shared services and burst GPU workloads make monthly invoices impossible to attribute.
must_address: commit only after measuring stable demand
trap: Reserved commitments do not fix unowned or idle resources.

title: Safe deployment
brief: A global API needs frequent releases, auditable change, and rollback within ten minutes.
trap: All-at-once production deployment conflicts with the rollback objective.

title: Business continuity
brief: A regional outage must preserve accepted jobs and resume processing without duplicate side effects.
trap: DNS failover alone neither moves state nor guarantees consistency.

title: Private regulated API
brief: A regulated workload must reach AWS services without public egress while resisting credential theft and web attacks.
trap: A private subnet is not private if routes and endpoints expose unintended paths.

title: Burst reliability
brief: Traffic bursts 20x and downstream processing occasionally fails or throttles.
trap: Scaling producers without backpressure can worsen downstream failure.

title: Latency architecture
brief: Global readers need p95 under 200 ms while writes require strong regional transaction semantics.
trap: A cache cannot be treated as the transactional source of truth.

title: Cost-aware design
brief: A new service has unpredictable launch traffic and large object storage with declining access.
trap: Buying maximum long-term capacity before measuring demand increases commitment risk.

title: Operations remediation
brief: Deployments are manual, alarms unactionable, and incidents recur without owners.
trap: Collecting more logs without decisions, ownership, or retention is not operational excellence.

title: Security improvement
brief: Long-lived keys, broad roles, inconsistent patches, and incomplete backups exist across accounts.
trap: Rotation alone does not correct excessive authorization.

title: Performance bottleneck
brief: Average latency is fine but p99 spikes during synchronized reads from distant users.
trap: Average CPU does not identify tail latency or network/data bottlenecks.

title: Reliability review
brief: A nominally Multi-AZ system still has one NAT path, one scheduler, and an untested failover.
trap: A Multi-AZ database does not make the entire system Multi-AZ.

title: FinOps improvement
brief: Spend rises 40% while usage is flat and ownership tags are missing.
trap: Spot Instances are not a universal remedy, particularly for non-interruptible workloads.

title: Portfolio selection
brief: Two hundred applications must be sequenced before a data-center exit with limited migration teams.
trap: Migrating in arbitrary server order ignores application dependencies.

title: Migration mechanism
brief: A 500-TB dataset, low-bandwidth site, transactional database, and federated identity must move with minimal outage.
trap: One transfer service does not fit bulk files, databases, applications, and identity.

title: Target platform
brief: A legacy application has shared files, relational transactions, stateless web nodes, and a nightly batch.
trap: Moving every component unchanged to one EC2 instance preserves failure and scaling constraints.

title: Modernization
brief: A monolith couples ingestion, notification, search, and reporting, causing synchronized scaling and fragile releases.
trap: Splitting code into services without independent data, failure, and deployment boundaries is not effective decoupling.
